subject: pol-dy
title: POL.DY.------PROG.CONT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-3 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan), first of two on book p245. Accompanies Braxton's argument: 'the planet expansion of post-Parker creativity can be viewed as related to the social-reality implications of the Second World War — and the subsequent interest (focus) on creative black music that solidified in that period profoundly affected the vibrational creative arena of both western Europe and Japan.' (C)POL-DY (the concept of political dynamics) is crossed with PROG-CONT (progressional continuance): the question is what political-dynamics produces when crossed with progressional-continuance — the political-dynamics here being the post-WW2 reordering that opened European and Japanese receptivity to creative black music. PROG-CONT sits at the upper-right. Three lines branch from the main line: a vertical up to SPT-DY (spiritual dynamics), which carries RIT-DY (ritual dynamics); CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics) on the right, which carries AF-DY (affinity dynamics), with INFO-DE (information degrees) hanging from AF-DY; and a long horizontal left to (R)INFO-DY (reality of information dynamics). From (R)INFO-DY a diagonal runs down to AFL (affinity alignment), which carries APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) and SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics); PART (participation) hangs from SOC-RT-DY at the lower-left.
